$comment: R8-P2-05: the VERSIONED object-namespace grammar, declared once and read by every language that needs it. Before this file the Rust adapter owned the layout and tools/maintenance/s3_gc.py owned a copy of its segment positions, so the maintenance tool covered only the legacy shape and would have silently mis-parsed the controller-derived one the moment that seam was wired. A copy of a layout is a layout that will disagree.

escape.$comment: The injective byte escaping fork/typedb/storage/keyspace/slate.rs::encode_segment_byte applies to every opaque segment. `=` is the ONLY escape, so distinct byte strings never share an encoding and decoding is unambiguous.

versions.$comment: What the local lanes produce today: object_prefix() derives the namespace from the host-local keyspace PATH, injectively encoded into a single segment beneath the root prefix. Its instability across checkout roots and hosts is the S-01 defect v2 exists to replace, which is exactly why a maintenance tool must still read it — the objects are already out there.
versions.$followed_by_comment: slate.rs::DB_SUBDIR. The SlateDB subtree sits under a literal `keyspace/` directory immediately after the namespace, in BOTH lanes. It is the segment that makes the two versions unambiguous rather than a heuristic about which one looks more likely.

versions.$comment: fork/typedb/storage/keyspace/slate.rs::MaterialisationNamespace::to_object_prefix. Every segment is a controller-owned opaque identifier, injectively encoded, so the same identity resolves to the same prefix on any machine. `status: declared` states the honest position: the struct is the typed seam, and TypeDB does not yet carry the controller identifiers down to it.
versions.$followed_by_comment: slate.rs::DB_SUBDIR. The SlateDB subtree sits under a literal `keyspace/` directory immediately after the namespace, in BOTH lanes. It is the segment that makes the two versions unambiguous rather than a heuristic about which one looks more likely.
